title: Aucly: flat-fee online auction platform for UK schools, PTAs and charities

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: Real auctions show an engaged named buyer: Furzedown Primary PTA ran a 7-day auction with 44 lots, 63 unique bidders and 1,074 bids; fundraising auctions recur annually for schools/PTAs. Dissatisfaction with incumbents is not evidenced, so the score is 3 rather than higher.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: The buyer is identifiable (PTA chair/committee, school fundraiser, small charity organiser) with budget authority over the event. Aucly's £60/£120 paid tiers and incumbent commission pricing show the budget line exists. The roughly seven paid auctions are owner-supplied and unverified, so this is not a 4.

evidence_strength.rationale: First-party operating evidence exists (live auctions, published case-study figures, production payment infrastructure, first-party analytics) rather than desk research. It is small, non-audited and silent on retention and market size, so 4 not 5; the payment count itself is unverified.

distribution.rationale: Negative primary evidence: a substantial SEO investment produced 45 GSC clicks and 2,333 recorded visitors in the export window with 0 accounts, 0 auctions launched and £0 revenue; queries are brand-dominated. No unpaid channel has demonstrated it can reach organisers, so the plausible-only cap applies.

differentiation.rationale: Flat fee with no commission and no bidder tips is a genuine difference, but it is contested by free plans (GalaBid, Jumblebee beeFree) and a scaled incumbent platform (PTA Events); no evidence that organisers switch for it. Direct incumbent overlap caps this at 2.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: The main open questions (unpaid acquisition, willingness to keep the flat fee) can be tested in 30 days with ~20 human hours and no spend via direct outreach with fixed kill rules. Nothing needs to be built.

feasibility.rationale: The product is built, deployed and running real auctions (Railway hosting, Stripe/offline payments, Brevo email, post-sale workflows). Feasibility is demonstrated, though maintenance is a continuing founder-time burden.

economics.rationale: Flat £0/£60/£120 one-off pricing caps revenue per organiser per event; with roughly seven unverified paid auctions, per-auction contribution after hosting, email and founder time is not quantified. Modelled-only economics cap at 2.

founder_fit.rationale: The founder has built and continuously operates the product, shipping a broad feature set and handling real customer workflows; this is evidenced execution fit. Domain access, sales capacity and time-to-value for the founder are not evidenced.

risk.rationale: No regulated data and no funds held by Aucly, but competition from entrenched platforms, dependency on email/hosting providers and a small market remain live risks. No unacceptable legal/privacy/trust risk identified.

economic_buyer.note: PTA/school/charity organisers control the event budget and already pay for auction platforms in the category (commission or managed services); Aucly's own paid tiers exist at £60/£120.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Fundraising auctions are a recurring annual job for schools/PTAs, and the recorded Furzedown auction shows engaged organisers and bidders (44 lots, 63 unique bidders, 1,074 bids, £2,265 raised).

non_paid_distribution.note: No unpaid channel has produced measurable accounts: the recorded export window shows 2,333 visitors and 0 accounts created. Direct outreach is untested.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: aucly-channel-test: 20 direct unpaid contacts; proceeds only if at least 2 launch a real auction within 30 days at zero paid spend

defensible_wedge.note: Flat fee with no commission is a real difference but contestable (GalaBid free plan, Jumblebee beeFree, PTA Events' scale); no evidence organisers switch for it.
defensible_wedge.resolve_via: win/loss conversations in aucly-channel-test asking which platform organisers use today, what it costs them and whether the flat fee changed their decision

no_network_effects_needed.note: A single organiser runs an auction for their own invited community; Furzedown's 63 bidders came from one PTA. No marketplace density is required.

plausible_margins.note: £60/£120 per auction against Railway hosting, Brevo email and continuing founder maintenance; per-auction contribution is not quantified.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: record actual hosting/email cost and founder hours per launch and per auction, and whether organisers return in a second year

acceptable_risk.note: No regulated data beyond organiser/bidder contact details; payments normally run through the organiser's own Stripe or bank transfer and Aucly does not hold funds. Remaining risks are commercial, not legal or trust risks.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A 20-contact unpaid outreach test with a pre-fixed kill rule can disconfirm the distribution assumption in 30 days at about 20 human hours and no spend.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability still requires unpaid acquisition, repeat usage, adequate market size and workable founder-time economics; several assumptions (A3, A5-A7) remain untested.
not_all_optimistic.resolve_via: run aucly-channel-test and a retention/pricing follow-up; if no repeatable unpaid route emerges, park or kill
